title: TimeSAE: Causal Sparse Decoding for Faithful Explanations of Black-Box Time Series Models
claim: A black-box explainer is built from a sparse concept autoencoder, trained with counterfactual interventions and a consistency objective for faithful explanations.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, each with encoder/decoder boxes and a black-box model
description: Three gray rounded panels, labeled A, B and C, sit side by side. Panel A, Time Sparse Autoencoder, runs top to bottom. A time series x enters an Explainer encoder, which produces a pill of colored concept icons (circle, triangle, hexagon, diamond). A Decoder g reconstructs x̃, which feeds a dark Blackbox Model f with a lock icon. The output ỹ goes to a Label-Fidelity box, with a ground-truth node y beside it. A legend explains the hammer (intervention), the inactive gray concept and the active green concept. Panel B, Causal Intervention, shows two parallel branches. One uses the original concepts. The other uses concepts changed by a hammer. Each passes through g and the black box, and a Contrastive loss L_cf compares the outputs. A green check marks Faithfulness (Theorem 1). Panel C, Compositional Consistency, shows concepts recombined and passed through the encoder and decoder in a loop, with a consistency loss L_cc. A check marks the Consistency Objective (Eq. 10). Gray trapezoids and the black boxes anchor the eye, and colored concept icons add accents.
caption: Overview of Time Series Sparse Autoencoder (\modelname): (A) The framework assumes access to a black-box model $f$ and aims to explain its predictions on data $\rvx \in \gX$ by learning an encoder $\gE$ and a decoder $\decoder$ that decompose the time series into interpretable components. (B) For faithfulness, the sparse autoencoder $(\gE, \decoder)$ incorporates properties to leverage counterfactual explanations. A contrastive learning loss incorporates a set of counterfactuals $\tilde{\rvx}^{cf}$, obtained by intervening on concepts and which produce, via $f$, a contradictory label $\tilde{\rvy}^{cf}$ relative to the original $\tilde{\rvy}$. (C) To ensure compositional explanations, the method enforces the encoder $\gE$ to generate consistent explanations by combining intermediate findings.
abstract: As black box models and pretrained models gain traction in time series applications, understanding and explaining their predictions becomes increasingly vital, especially in high-stakes domains where interpretability and trust are essential. However, most of the existing methods involve only in-distribution explanation, and do not generalize outside the training support, which requires the learning capability of generalization. In this work, we aim to provide a framework to explain black-box models for time series data through the dual lenses of Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) and causality. We show that many current explanation methods are sensitive to distributional shifts, limiting their effectiveness in real-world scenarios. Building on the concept of Sparse Autoencoder, we introduce TimeSAE, a framework for black-box model explanation. We conduct extensive evaluations of TimeSAE on both synthetic and real-world time series datasets, comparing it to leading baselines. The results, supported by both quantitative metrics and qualitative insights, show that TimeSAE provides more faithful and robust explanations. Our code is available in an easy-to-use library TimeSAE-Lib: https://oublalkhalid.github.io/TimeSAE/
